metadata.title: SOPP 8005 Formal Dispute Resolution Process
metadata.edition: 8005 · listed on the FDA SOPP page, 2026-11-26
metadata.legal_basis: CBER Standard Operating Procedure and Policy (internal FDA procedure). Informative; not binding on applicants.

metadata_verification: Source-register metadata; dates and legal status require human verification.
limitations: English rule-based extraction; no GPT or paid API.
Candidates are not approved requirements. Read the original, qualifications and exceptions.

candidates.statement: G. If a meeting or teleconference must take place to discuss the formal review of any FDA decisions or actions taken on a CBER medical device submission, the meetings will be scheduled as a Submission Issue Meeting as described in the Guidance for Industry and Food and Drug Administration Staff: Requests for Feedback and Meetings for Medical Device Submissions: The Q-Submission Program . For human drug or biological applications (i.e., BLAs and NDAs) covered by PDUFA a Type A meeting will be scheduled as described in Guidance for Industry: Formal Meetings Between the FDA and Sponsors or Applicants of PDUFA Products .
candidates.context: F. For FDRRs involving applications not subject to PDUFA, or those related to applications or submissions for CBER-regulated medical devices covered under the Medical Device User Fee Act (MDUFA), the timelines described in this SOPP will be met as resources permit. F. After any type of response letter regarding the FDRR has been issued by CBER, the review clock is stopped. Upon official receipt of a complete response submitted by the sponsor, the review clock is reset to day zero and restarted.

candidates.statement: G. Clarifying information must not include new information or reanalysis of data that has not been reviewed by the division. The FDA considers new analyses of previously reviewed data to be new information
candidates.context: F. After any type of response letter regarding the FDRR has been issued by CBER, the review clock is stopped. Upon official receipt of a complete response submitted by the sponsor, the review clock is reset to day zero and restarted. because the original deciding official might have made a different decision had they had the opportunity to review the new analysis.

candidates.statement: H. If the decision is to disagree with the FDRR, (i.e., Deciding Official agrees with the FDA staff that made the initial decision), the response must include the reasons for the disagreement and, where applicable, any additional action available to the sponsor to continue pursuit of the appeal.
candidates.context: because the original deciding official might have made a different decision had they had the opportunity to review the new analysis.

candidates.statement: c. Inform the sponsor that if proceeding with an FDRR, they must submit that formal dispute resolution request under the parent application if the dispute pertains to an active regulatory submission and a copy should be sent to the CBER Ombudsman.
candidates.context: b. Provide the CBER Ombudsman contact information, available at Contact an Ombudsman at FDA . B. Receive the FDRR from the Document Control Center. [CBER Ombudsman]

candidates.statement: i. Issue a letter or email to the sponsor acknowledging receipt and acceptance of the FDRR. The communication should include the following:
candidates.context: a. If the FDRR satisfies the procedural criteria described in Section IV of the Guidance, accept the FDRR and start the 30-day review clock from the date of CBER’s receipt. a) The date the FDRR was received. b) The name of the Deciding Official assigned to review the FDRR.

candidates.statement: I. If a meeting with the sponsor is required to address the issue(s): [Deciding Official]
candidates.context: 3. Include consultative review comments in the documentation for the FDRR. 1. For biological products, schedule it as a Type A Meeting. Refer to SOPP 8101.1: Regulatory Meetings with Sponsors and Applicants for Drugs and Biological Products .

candidates.statement: 2. Prepare year-end summary reports and status reports on all PDUFA related FDRs for inclusion in the Report to Congress. The reports should include statistics on FDRs accepted, resolved, granted, and denied, as well as average resolution timeframes.
candidates.context: 1. Provide an update every 6 months on all active PDUFA related FDRs to the CBER RIB. [CBER Ombuds] [RIB in consultation with CBER Ombudsman]
